title: Word 7 — On the Calamity of a Christian Who Lives Lawlessly After Holy Baptism
attribution_note: Word 7 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The blessedness lost through lawless living

pairs.en: It is impossible to describe fully, or sufficiently to lament, the calamitous state of a Christian who, after holy Baptism, has given himself over to lawless deeds and lives lawlessly. He is deprived of all the blessedness he was granted by God's grace at his baptism, and he willfully casts himself back into that very calamity from which he had been delivered — indeed, into a still greater calamity. For he had come to know the truth, but did not wish to live in it; he had come to know God, but did not wish to honor Him; he had come to know the path leading to eternal blessedness, but did not wish to walk it; he had promised to serve God, but lied to Him in this; he had been washed, sanctified, and justified, but has lost all of this; he had become a child of God, but has lost this most glorious nobility; he had become an heir of eternal life and the Kingdom, but has squandered that inheritance. For this reason the apostle says of such people: *“It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them”* [2 Peter 2:21].

sections.heading: A calamity hidden now, revealed at the Judgment

pairs.en: You see, O Christian, what a calamity it is for a Christian to live lawlessly! It is not visible now, for it is perceived not with bodily eyes but with the eyes of the soul. But it will be made manifest when all our deeds, hidden and open alike, are revealed to the whole world — that is, at the second coming of Christ. Then that poor Christian will know and see his great misfortune and ruin.

Truly, many tears and much weeping are needed to lament the condition of such a Christian. As one who has washed in the bathhouse soils himself again with filth and dung, so the Christian who has been washed in the bath of Baptism defiles himself again with lawless deeds. Everyone who lives lawlessly after holy Baptism acts like a man who, having exchanged his filthy rags for purple and fine linen, strips off that beautiful garment again and puts his loathsome rags back on; for he too had put on the robe of Christ's justification in place of the rags of sin, but, casting off that beautiful garment, has clothed himself again in the rags of sin. He acts just like one who, having come out of darkness into the light, returns again into darkness — for he had come out of the darkness of sin into the light of Christ, the true Light, but has turned back again into the darkness of sin. As one freed from slavery and captivity comes out into liberty and then returns again into that bitter bondage, so the Christian who lives lawlessly had been delivered by Christ's grace from the bitter slavery and captivity of the devil, but has returned again into that calamity. As a man freed from a deep pit falls back into that same pit, so the Christian who lives lawlessly had been drawn up out of the pit of eternal ruin, but has willfully thrown himself back into that pit. To him happens what the true proverb says: *“The dog returns to his own vomit, and the sow that was washed returns to wallowing in the mire”* [2 Peter 2:22].
To all such people happens what the true proverb says: *“The dog returns to his own vomit, and the sow that was washed returns to wallowing in the mire.”*

Beloved Christians, washed in the bath of holy Baptism! Let us look at ourselves, and see whether any of us has turned back from Christ to the devil, and has fallen into the calamitous state described above. Whoever does the works of the devil has turned back to the devil and serves him, and has already fallen away from Christ. Woe to Christians who live lawlessly after holy Baptism! *“It will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment”* [Matthew 10:15] than for such Christians. Poor Christian! Examine yourself and take heed, lest you become an eternal captive of the devil and of perdition, *“where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.”* O God, spare Your rational creature, made according to Your own image! Amen.
